Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

2. During the hearing of these petitions, a disturbing facet has emerged whereby the Deputy Collector, Land Acquisition, Metro Center No.1 - Mr Dattatray Nawale, has filed four affidavits and has taken a completely different stand in at least two of them.

This led us to pass an order on 7 March 2024, which is as follows:
".
Amendment as per draft amendment is granted.
Amendment to be carried out before the next date and notice be given to the added Respondent.

2. Dispute that is raised before us is a short one as to whether Survey No. 59/8 admeasuring 3H-72R-3P in Village Asudgaon, Taluka- Panvel, District -Raigad has been acquired by the State Government or not.
This question has to be answered by the State Government - Acquiring Authority based on the record.

On this issue, we Sneha Chavan 3 86-WP-1983-23.doc have one affidavit of Mr.Dattatray R. Nawale,
Deputy Collector (Land Acquisition) Metro Center No. 1, Panvel dated 17 October 2022 which was filed after perusing the available record maintained in the office, and the Deponent is well conversant with the facts of the case.

He stated on oath as under :
"14.

I say that without publishing mandatory notification under Section 11 as required under Government Resolution dated 30.03.2016 which is required to determine the market value of the said land, the predecessor officer of Respondent No.2 passed the impugned Order dated 30.06.2011 wherein she calculated the amount of compensation at the rate of Rs. 17,200 per sq. meters and declared the total compensation Rs.71,08,76,000/- (Rupees Seventy One Crore Eight lakhs Seventy Six thousand only) out of which 50% advance compensation amounting to Rs.
35,54,38,000/- (Rupees Thirty-Five Crore Fifty-Four Lakh and Thirty-Eighth Thousand Only) was disbursed in three equal parts to Petitioners and Mr.Anand Puranik's amounting to Ranjit Anand Puranik vs The State Of Maharashtra Thr Government ... on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29696628/
2 Rs.11,85,79,334/- (Rupees Eleven Crore Eighty-Five Lakh and Seventy-Nine Thousand Three Hundred Thirty -Four Only).

sentences.text: The valuation of the acquired land is to be calculated as per the date to Notification published under section 11 of the Land Acquisition Act 2013 and it was published on 29.11.2018, 5 months after the impugned order dated 30.06.2018.

The erring/ predecessor officer of Respondent No.2 was aware that the Sneha Chavan 4 86-WP-1983-23.doc factual position of said land and custodia legis is with the Court Receiver of Hon'ble Bombay High Court and yet passed the impugned order dated 30.06.2018 which is not in conformity with the legal provisions and thus is arbitrary, irregular, defective and bad in law.
Hereto annexed and marked as "Exhibit -5" is a copy of the impugned order dated 30.06.2018 passed by the erring/ predecessor officer of Respondent No.2".

Thereafter, he stated on oath as under :
"25.I say that the entire acquisition proceeding has lapsed and there is no final award passed by the Respondent No.2.

Thus, said land is not required for the acquisition,
and as when Respondent No. 10 requires for the development of Navi Mumbai Development project it shall issue fresh proposal acquisition for the said land."

3. Thereafter, we have the second affidavit of Mr.Dattatray R. Nawale dated 15 December 2023 wherein he has stated that the Award of Survey No. 59/8 is not available and he has inferred from the available record that Survey No. 59/8 is already acquired by his office.
4. It is on the basis of these affidavits that the proceeding in writ jurisdiction has to be taken forward.
It is not expected from the authorities of the State Government to file such casual affidavits changing their stand.

5. We, therefore, direct Mr. Dattatray Nawale to remain present in the Court on the next date of hearing to explain as to why this Court should not consider that filing such conflicting affidavits as an attempt to mislead this Court.

6. Stand over to 14 March 2024 at 2.30 p.m."
Sneha Chavan 5 86-WP-1983-23.doc 3.
The concerned Officer is present in the Court.

We are not getting any satisfactory answers, except to state that the affidavit filed on 17 October 2022 was based on the record available, and subsequent affidavits are filed after examining the record thoroughly.
The Writ Petition could have been disposed of on the basis of the affidavit dated 17 October 2022.
4. We find that this conduct of the concerned Officer is bordering on misleading the Court.
The foundation of writ jurisdiction is on the affidavits.
Petitions may be adjudicated and orders may be issued solely on the basis of these affidavits.
This is particularly significant when considering affidavits submitted by State Officers, as they are obligated to present accurate and truthful information.
Under the Evidence Act, there is a presumption to acts of the State.

sentences.text: Surely the State will not permit its officers to submit casual affidavits and alter their positions arbitrarily.
Therefore, apart from the action that the Court may take, this is also a case that the superiors of the concerned Officer should look into.

5. While we permit the said Deputy Collector to file an affidavit to explain the position, let this order and all four affidavits filed by said Officer in this petition be placed before the Principal Secretary,
Revenue Department, State of Maharashtra, Sneha Chavan 6 86-WP-1983-23.doc to look into the same and to examine whether any action is warranted.
The office of the Government Pleader will send copies of the four affidavits to the Secretary of the Revenue Department.
We expect the Secretary's response by the next date.
6. Response of the Deputy Collector to be filed before the next date.
Stand over to 8 April 2024.
7. We make it clear that we will independently examine the dispute between the private parties before us.
Our anxiety in passing this order is to uphold and protect the purity of the Court process.
